newsitem.title: UK: Scottish jobs at risk as mine put on flood alert.
newsitem.headline: Scottish jobs at risk as mine put on flood alert.

text.p: Scores of jobs were put at risk on Friday when water started gushing into Waverley Mining Finance Plc's Monktonhall colliery near Edinburgh, leading to the suspension of operations.
Water is flooding the mine from a broad area at a rate of 1,250 gallons per minute, Waverley said. The company is drilling a borehole to make a more accurate assessment of the extent of the damage.
In the meantime, staffing levels, totalling some 300, are being severely scaled back while the mine has been temporarily placed on a care and maintenance basis.
"The management of Monktonhall will detail sufficient numbers of men to safely manage the colliery and the de-watering operations," Waverley Mining said in a statement.
Experts say in excess of 100 jobs are likely to be retained during de-watering.
The company said a clearer picture of the mine's problems would emerge next week after the results from the bore hole survey show the full extent of the problem.

Most deep pits experience some flooding. Monktonhall, Britain's deepest remaining site, had seen water seep in at an average of 250 gallons per minute before it started gushing into the pit over the last 10 days.
Monktonhall was saved from closure in 1992 when 160 miners mortgaged their homes to invest 1.6 million pounds at 10,000 a share to buy the former British Coal mine.

Waverley, which said it expected the mine to able to achieve "satisfactory levels of production...subject to the resolution of the water difficulties", has fully owned the mine since December 1995, when it bought a remaining 51 percent stake from Monktonhall Mineworkers.
The company is developing a second coal face at the mine.
